text: The Long Man of Wilmington is a chalk figure on a hill in East Sussex. He is drawn as a man who holds two long staves. The white-cut image rises some 226 feet from the ground. He stands taller than the Giant of Cerne, though he lacks that figure's bold carving. No sure date or maker is known for him. The shape may mark some old god of the Celts or of an earlier people. One tale says the lines were traced around a real giant laid to rest on the slope.

okr.objective: Set out the size, form, and mystery of the Long Man of Wilmington.
